nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Collaboration with ngos_qna_000
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What role do multi-lateral agencies, civil society groups, and research institutions play in the context of MIs and the UPF industry?
nodes.answer: They provide legitimacy to the interests of corporations within the UPF industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Collaboration with ngos_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: According to the paragraph, why might governments, businesses, and civil society organizations partner in sustainable development?
nodes.answer: They may partner because underregulation of global economic interrelationships has led to negative socioeconomic and environmental circumstances, highlighting the importance of collaborative efforts.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Collaboration with ngos_qna_002
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can NGOs and trade unions contribute to supplier governance?
nodes.answer: NGOs and trade unions can facilitate sharing knowledge and resources between brands and suppliers, which can enhance collaboration and improve supplier governance practices according to Brunet al. (2020).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable supply chains|Collaboration with ngos_qna_003
nodes.question: How is the new multi-country collaboration attempting to address the sustainability of natural resource supply chains?
nodes.answer: The new multi-country collaboration aims to link international trade systems to social and environmental impacts to help bend the curve of biodiversity loss at scale.
